How MUSE joins tissue slices, one idea at a time

Adjacent slices of one tissue disagree: each was imaged in its own frame, and some are much sparser than others. MUSE matches their spots with optimal transport, then lets the denser slice help the sparser one. The toy below runs on two small slices modeled on a DLPFC section; boxes marked Paper quote the paper.

Match spots by expression and by distances that agree

minT (1 − α) Σ δ(xi(A), xj′(B)) Tij′ + α Σ (Dip(A) − Dj′q′(B))2 Tij′ Tpq′

The first term pairs spots with similar expression (δ is a KL divergence). The second keeps relative distances: if i goes to j′ and p to q′, the distance i–p in A should match j′–q′ in B, measured in each slice’s own coordinates. Slice A is colored by position; each spot of B takes the color of the A spot it is matched to. Slide α and watch the pattern carry over.

expression onlydistances only
B spots matched into the same layer
Distance to the true spot, in spot spacings

Paper α = 0.8 by default; the transport plan T is solved with the conditional gradient method and keeps every spot’s mass (rows sum to ai, columns to bj′). On two human DLPFC slices (151673 to 151674) most spots map to the same annotated layer, and the misses fall mostly into the neighboring layer. At the lowest quality level, with 93.75% of the non-zero entries masked, transport accuracy stays at 0.60 with the KL cost, against 0.13 with a PCA-based Euclidean cost (Fig. 5A, Fig. 3B).

Let a sparse spot borrow its matched spot from the dense slice

i = argmaxi Tij′,   Nj′ ← Nj′original ∪ { xi(A) }

A graph method describes each spot through its neighbourhood. When slice B is sparse, the neighbourhood is sparse too. MUSE adds one virtual neighbor per spot: the A spot it is best aligned with. Thin slice B the way the paper builds its quality levels, then tap a spot to see what its neighbourhood carries.

What the selected spot’s neighbourhood carries

Every spot of B, by quality level

Paper STAGATE on slice 151673 (reference 151674), Q1 to Q4: on its own its domain accuracy falls from 0.55 to 0.03 ARI and its imputation error rises from 0.67 to 1.32 RMSE; inside MUSE it keeps 0.58 to 0.37 ARI and 0.58 to 0.90 RMSE. At Q4, the virtual neighbors alone bring the imputation error from 1.32 to 0.93; for domains the alignment loss matters more (Tables 2–3, Fig. 3A).

Toy: the same slices; as in the paper (Sec. 3.5), quality level Q1 masks a random 50% of B’s non-zero entries, Q2 75%, Q3 87.5% and Q4 93.75% (each level keeps part of the one before), and B is re-aligned at α = 0.8 each time. “Signal” is the cosine similarity between the mean normalized profile of the spot and its six graph neighbours (plus the virtual neighbor when added) and the true profile of the spot’s layer. Bars group the 200 genes into the seven layers’ marker blocks and the rest.

Pull slice B’s embedding toward the spots it is matched to

ℒ(B) = (1 − β) ℒoriginal(B) + β ℒalign(B),   ℒalign(B) = φ(H(A), T H(B))

MUSE keeps an existing single-slice encoder–decoder and adds one loss. Trained alone, slice B’s embedding lands in a space of its own: the layers form clusters, but not where A’s are. The alignment loss asks each A spot’s embedding to match the transport-weighted mix of its B partners. Move β and the toy encoder is solved again.

B on its ownalignment only
B spots whose nearest A spot shares their layer
Reconstruction loss of B
Alignment loss

Paper φ is the mean squared error and β = 0.5 by default. The encoder–decoder is the one of the method MUSE wraps (SpaceFlow, STAGATE, GraphST, stCluster or Impeller), trained on each slice’s own graph; at Q4 on 151673, the alignment loss alone lifts STAGATE’s domain accuracy from 0.03 to 0.36 ARI (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 3A).

Toy: a linear encoder from B’s top 20 principal components to 2 dimensions and a linear decoder back, solved by alternating least squares from B’s own orientation; A’s embedding is its own 2-D PCA, held fixed as the reference. The loss values have no units.

Toys, not results: the slices are small simulations of a DLPFC section (the paper’s data come from Maynard et al., 2021), computed with the paper’s objective (Eqs. 1, 4 and 5). MUSE: Duan et al., CIKM 2025.
